You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from Riverview Task 1 2026 (a Riverview Year 12 Business Studies assessment, Operations topic) strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 12(a) [2 marks]: Using an example, outline how the quality expectations of customers would influence the outputs of operations for this business.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
A business sells ice-creams and enjoys a prime position on a popular beach front. Sales have increased on weekends and school holidays due to a viral social media post highlighting the large selection of flavours and toppings.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 2):
2 marks: Sketches in general terms how the quality expectations would influence outputs
1 marks: Makes a statement about quality expectations or outputs like customer service

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Quality expectations refers to the pre-existing idea about the quality of the product based on experience or marketing by the customer. This has a significant impact on the outputs of this business: due to the social media campaign, customers expect excellent customer service from staff that are friendly and knowledgeable and a variety of high-quality flavours and toppings that differentiate their output from their competitors.


TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
The most common reason students did not receive 2/2 is that they failed to adequately reference the way the quality expectations would influence the outputs. Some answers displayed circular reasoning (because customers expect a large variety of flavours, they need to produce a large variety of flavours), which is self-evident and did not demonstrate understanding of the outputs part of the course. Some students forgot to reference the ice cream business, which was a requirement of the question (this business).


STUDENT RESPONSE:
"""

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-2>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '2'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a full-mark answer in 2 to 5 plain sentences a student could realistically write in the exam>"}
